recommended_manifest_writes.evidence_direction_note_append: 2026-07-20 (failure autopsy, V3-EXQ-728): SUPERSEDED. Established by code archaeology, not inference: the run executed against driver commit c83221c, whose _train_all_on_agent carries the same three optimizer groups as HEAD (e2, lateral-PFC bias head, OFC devaluation head), none covering any latent_stack parameter -- 'latent_stack' appears zero times in that revision -- with the same latent.z_world.detach() at the P0 buffer; git diff c83221c..HEAD on the driver shows zero changed torch.optim lines, the only intervening commits being the pack_writer manifest-writing migration. The guarded 2026-07-20 re-run measured 0 of 4 world_encoder and 0 of 61 latent_stack tensors changed on that identical training path, 3 of 3 seeds. Near-identical metrics across the two runs corroborate (foraging 0.167 vs 0.117, goal_reach 0.117 vs 0.10, planning_depth 1.33 vs 1.42). The interpretation_label 'trained_allon_capability_point_landed' is therefore FALSE: no trained all-ON capability point was landed. Superseded by the post-fix re-run gated on sd_zworld_warmup_optimizer_group. Nothing in claims.yaml moves (claim_ids empty, non_contributory, baseline). NOTE a compounding recording gap: this manifest is missing 6 always-core fields (recording_schema, TOP-LEVEL substrate_hash, machine_class, elapsed_seconds, config, seeds) per ree-v3/validate_recording.py. Its per-arm arm_fingerprint blocks DO carry substrate_hash values, but a whole-glob hash only tells you the substrate differed, never whether the optimizer defect was present -- so driver-code archaeology was necessary regardless, and the missing always-core is what removed the cheap first-pass check. SECOND, INDEPENDENT GROUND FOR SUPERSESSION (added 2026-07-20 on re-read): those per-arm hashes are NOT CONSISTENT WITHIN THE RUN -- two distinct values across the nine arms. efc51d920ab8 covers all three random_walk arms plus ree_trained_allon seed 42; 0ba1115de45a covers ree_trained_allon seeds 43 and 44 plus all three greedy_oracle arms. So the floor and ceiling anchors were measured against a different substrate than part of the treatment arm, and the normalized positions are cross-substrate comparisons. This is the cardinality>1 signature that substrate_stable_across_run / arm_reuse.source_run_substrate_unstable() (ree-v3 a23f189, landed 2026-07-20) exists to catch, so the run is now refusable as a reuse source. Read with the caveat that entry states in its own scope note: a moved whole-glob hash counts a changed RECORDED VALUE, not a demonstrated loss of experimental control (_SUBSTRATE_GLOBS is wider than what any run imports). It is therefore corroborating, not independently dispositive -- but it is a second defect on the same capability point and it points the same way.

learning_extracted: The guard's first real dividend is a RETROSPECTIVE one. Its detection value was argued prospectively (737a), but its larger payoff here was licensing a re-read of an already-reviewed PASS: the 07-09 capability point had cleared review, closed a plan work-stream, and would never have re-surfaced. A detector that fires on a new run should trigger an audit of every prior run on the same code path, not just adjudication of the run it fired on.

Code archaeology beats metric similarity for retrospective invalidation, and the two should be reported in that order. The near-identical numbers across the 07-09 and 07-20 runs are suggestive but circumstantial; 'git diff c83221c..HEAD shows zero changed torch.optim lines and latent_stack appears zero times in the older revision' is dispositive. Where a manifest lacks substrate_hash, driver-commit archaeology is the fallback that still yields a hard answer.

A missing always-core substrate_hash removes the cheap FIRST-PASS check, but it was never going to be the dispositive one -- state that precisely rather than as 'unrecoverable'. The 07-09 manifest lacks the top-level field yet its per-arm fingerprints carry hashes; a whole-glob hash still could not have answered whether the optimizer defect was present, so archaeology was required either way. The Experimental Recording Standard's value here is triage speed, not sufficiency.

Re-reading a manifest for ONE question surfaced a second, unrelated defect -- read the whole artifact, not the field you came for. Checking substrate_hash availability on the 07-09 run exposed intra-run substrate divergence (two distinct hashes across nine arms, with the floor/ceiling anchors on a different substrate than part of the treatment arm) that no one had looked for because the run was a PASS and already reviewed. A reviewed PASS is exactly where nobody re-reads.

An instrument landing today can retroactively flag a run from eleven days ago, and nothing sweeps for that automatically. substrate_stable_across_run / source_run_substrate_unstable() (a23f189) was built as a forward-looking reuse gate; applied backwards by hand it immediately caught the 07-09 run. New detectors deserve one deliberate backward sweep over the corpus they can now see, not just forward enforcement.

'Substrate not ready' and 'test design defective' produce the SAME self-route label and must be separated by whether the instrument stayed sound. V3-EXQ-786 was rejected on this label a week earlier; the discriminator here was that the guard was arm-scoped (anchors stayed green and scored), the env precondition passed independently at 6.3x the floor, and the defect was locatable in code across two independent drivers. A self-route label is a hypothesis about cause; the adjudication is what tests it.

A plan work-stream marked DONE on the strength of a specific run inherits that run's validity, and nothing re-checks it. WS-3 went DONE on 2026-07-09 citing V3-EXQ-728; when the run was invalidated 11 days later nothing propagated. Plan status rows citing a run_id should be treated as derived artifacts of that run's standing.

An unstamped bears_on silently zeroes a governance counter. 737a is fully GOV-DIAG-1-eligible and contributes nothing because the field is absent -- and the first strike is outside the corpus shape entirely, being a .md rather than a failure_autopsy_*.json. The rule is non-falsifying-safe by design, so the shortfall is invisible unless written down.
